title: An arrow's parts live in Appearance, each with its own colour
goal: An arrow has a line, a head and a caption pill, and the pill has a fill, an edge and its text. Right now one colour drives the line and the head together, the pill's colours are worked out from that colour rather than chosen, and the settings are split between Appearance and a separate arrow pane. Put an arrow's parts in Appearance like every other shape's parts: the line, the head, and the pill's fill, edge and text, each switchable where that makes sense and each with a colour set the way every other colour in the app is set. Fold the separate arrow pane in, so one section says how the thing looks.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-09. What the model has today, from Sources/PhotonzCore/Layer.swift: an annotation carries ONE colorHex (line 99) used for the shaft and the head, an optional fillColorHex (line 139) for a closed shape's interior, and the caption pill has no colours of its own at all: captionChipColor (line 329) darkens colorHex by 0.55 and keeps darkening until white text reads on it, and captionBorderWidth (line 357) is derived from strokeWidth. So giving the pill its own fill, edge and text colours is a model change, not just a panel change, and it needs a migration that turns an existing arrow's derived colours into stored ones so nothing shifts on opening. The colour slots that exist are fill, stroke, text, border and shadow (ColorStyles.swift line 26 onwards), which is nearly enough but does not distinguish a line from a head, so the parts model in LayerParts.swift is where the new parts belong rather than a sixth slot. The separate arrow section is the .annotation case in the inspector (Sources/Photonz/AnnotationInspector.swift, listed in InspectorSections.swift); folding it in means the shape settings that are not colours, the head style, the thickness, the caption roundness, need homes in Appearance too, so say where each went. This is the same principle as the Appearance and Effects split already agreed: Appearance says what the thing is made of.
acceptance: Appearance lists an arrow's parts: the line, the head, and the caption pill's fill, its edge and its text
Each of those has its own colour, chosen the same way every other colour in the app is chosen, including using and saving named colours
Setting the line's colour no longer changes the head, and setting the head's no longer changes the line
The pill's colours are chosen rather than derived from the line's colour, and the audit says what an existing arrow's pill becomes so nothing changes appearance on opening
There is no separate arrow section: everything that was in it is in Appearance, and the audit lists where each control went
An arrow with no caption shows no pill parts, so the section never offers settings for something that is not there
The white text on a dark pill that the old derivation guaranteed is not silently lost: if a chosen pair would be unreadable the audit says how that is handled
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the change, including an arrow saved before this opening unchanged
Audit written under queue/audits/ with an arrow with and without a caption, and a line and head in different colours, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Five colour rows on one arrow is a wall of controls, so the three label rows only exist once the arrow HAS a caption: a plain arrow shows Opacity, Line, Head, Caption, which is fewer controls than today's Appearance plus Annotation sections. (2) Biggest risk: cutting the line/head link means every existing way to recolour an arrow leaves the head behind. Keeping the paint bucket (Fill.swift) painting the whole arrow, because that gesture means 'make this thing this colour', not 'set the line'. (3) The old derivation guaranteed white text on a dark pill; once the colours are chosen that guarantee is gone, so the derivation becomes the SEED (nobody lands on white-on-white by default) and a legibility note appears under the label rows when the pair goes unreadable. (4) A caption's WORDS are content, not appearance, but a section holding one field is worse than folding it in, so the Caption field moves into Appearance and this is recorded as a known compromise. (5) An arrow that ends in nothing offers no Head row, so the panel never offers a colour for something invisible. (6) Shortest version: no width control for the pill's edge (still follows the arrow's thickness), no gradients on the pill, no new home for Reset label position.

Plan: AnnotationContent gains headPaint, captionFill, captionBorder, captionTextColorHex; ColorSlot gains arrowHead, captionFill, captionBorder, captionText; LayerPart gains captionFill and captionBorder as switchable parts; Appearance rows gain settings drawers (OwnedSettings) carrying Thickness, Ending, Head Size, Caption, Label size, Label corners; AnnotationInspector shows nothing under next-shape-parts.

Built. Model: AnnotationContent gained headPaint (the head's own colour), captionFill, captionBorder and captionTextColorHex. `caption` became a computed property so that EVERY way of putting words on an arrow seeds the label's three colours from the derivation that used to run at draw time, at the moment the label comes into being. Migration: an arrow decoded without a headColorHex key takes its line's colour; an arrow with a caption and no captionTextColorHex takes the exact three colours it used to draw. captionTextColorHex is the mark because it is the one of the three nobody can switch off.

ColorSlot gained arrowHead, captionFill, captionBorder, captionText, so every one of them goes down the same well, the same saved-colours menu and the same naming field every other colour does. captionFill and captionBorder are switchable like a box's fill; the head and the label's words are not. The label's slots exist only while the arrow has words; the head's only while it ends in something.

Panel: the arrow section is gone under next-shape-parts and every one of its controls moved into Appearance under the part it belongs to. Thickness under Line; Ending and Head Size under Head; the words, Label size and Label corners under a Caption block; Reset label position at the end of the section. Written down in the ShapePartSettings.swift header table and in docs/design/shape-parts.md.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the probe app. The first build hung the Head row off the head's COLOUR, so picking the plain ending took away the Ending picker you had just used: arrow-endings-walk failed in ten seconds. Fixed by making Head a part row that is there for every arrow with only its colour coming and going, and pinned by a test. Second finding: the Caption block's heading and the field's own label both said Caption, two lines apart, so the field's label is off in Appearance.

Verified: Scripts/test.sh green (5396 tests, 451 suites). New walk Scripts/playtest/arrow-parts-walk.json passes and carries a real screen capture at each stage (Screen Recording granted). Walks run: arrow* (16), caption* (11), part* (6), appearance* (3), colour* (12), style* (10), version* (6) - all pass. A full sweep was requested rather than run, because the Appearance row list and the stroke row's name changed under many walks.

Porting rule: PhotonzCore and PhotonzRender are shared, so the current release opens these documents too and draws them identically. Its Color section is deliberately NOT given the four new rows (EditorState.colorRowSlots filters them while next-shape-parts is off), so nothing about the current release changes.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-arrow-parts.json with four real screen captures.

Appearance now lists an arrow's parts (Line, Head, Caption, Label Fill, Label Edge, Label Text), each with its own colour set the way every other colour is, and the separate arrow section is gone with every one of its controls folded in under the part it belongs to. Model in PhotonzCore (headPaint plus the label's three, seeded from the old derivation so existing arrows open unchanged), panel in Sources/Photonz/ShapePartSettings.swift, design in docs/design/shape-parts.md. Verified: Scripts/test.sh green (5396 tests), new walk arrow-parts-walk.json passes with real screen captures, plus the arrow, caption, part, appearance, colour, style and version walk sets. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-arrow-parts.json. A full sweep was requested.
